content: Analyze the SVG path by first counting all unique vertices and confirming the path is closed (last point connects to first). Then, systematically check for structural features: count sides, identify parallel sides, measure side lengths (visually or relatively), and note angles and symmetry axes. Compare these features directly to each option's definition—e.g., a kite has four vertices, two distinct pairs of adjacent equal sides, and one line of symmetry. Apply this stepwise: for the given path, vertices at (64,63), (44,63), (44,50), (64,50), (64,45), (85,57), (64,68) form seven points, but the path closes at (64,63). Observe two pairs of equal adjacent sides and asymmetrical angles, matching a kite. For any new path, repeat: count vertices, check closure, then compare features to option criteria.
